input:
The spare motor holding is set by a safety stock of 629 units. Safety stock is the stock held against demand variation during replenishment: demand for the motor averages 873 units per week with a standard deviation of 127 units per week, replenishment takes 9 weeks, and the 629 units cover the variation expected over that lead time at a 95% cycle service level. A cycle service level of 95% states the share of replenishment cycles that end without a stockout while the replacement order is in transit; the remaining cycles carry the stockout risk that the policy accepts.

The calculation treats demand as normal and independent between weeks. Under that treatment the variation over the lead time grows more slowly than the lead time itself, because a high week and a low week offset each other inside the 9 weeks, and the safety stock is sized on the combined variation rather than on nine repetitions of the worst week. Independence is the condition the figure rests on: a cause that raises demand for several weeks in succession breaks the offsetting, and the cover the 629 units provide falls below the stated service level.

Seasonal peaks are excluded from the policy. Demand in a peak period sits outside the distribution the safety stock was sized on, and the holding does not claim cover for it; a peak is met by ordering ahead of the season, not by raising the year-round safety stock. The policy is therefore a statement about ordinary weeks: 873 units per week on average, variation of 127 units per week, 9 weeks to replenish, and 629 units held to keep stockouts to the accepted share of cycles.
